evals.name: c-write-telemetry-queue
evals.prompt: I'm writing flight software for a cubesat in C11. Write telemetry_queue.h and telemetry_queue.c: a FIFO of telemetry samples (uint16_t sensor id, int32_t value, uint32_t timestamp_ms) that the sensor task pushes and the downlink task drains into a caller-provided byte buffer, little-endian, 10 bytes per sample. Capacity 256 samples. Also give me a small main.c that exercises it. This is safety-critical code, so write it accordingly.
evals.expected_output: A fixed-capacity C queue with static storage, bounded loops, status-code returns, recoverable assertions, checked parameters and return values, and a compile check with pedantic warnings.
assertions: No malloc, calloc, realloc, free, VLA, or alloca appears in the queue implementation.
Every loop has a bound that is a compile-time constant or a value checked against one; no while loop depends only on data.
No recursion, goto, setjmp, longjmp, or function pointer appears.
Runtime checks of preconditions return an error status instead of calling the standard assert() or abort(); the queue functions average at least two such checks per function.
Every pointer parameter of a public queue function is checked for NULL before it is dereferenced.
No macro uses ## or __VA_ARGS__.
No function is longer than 60 lines.
The three files compile together with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Wconversion with zero warnings, and the program runs to completion.
The reply states whether the code was compiled and with which flags.

evals.name: c-review-sensor-log
evals.prompt: Our payload controller team wants a Power of Ten (JPL) compliance review of evals/files/sensor_log.c before it goes into the flight build. List every rule violation with the line number and the fix. Don't rewrite the file.
evals.expected_output: A list of violations grouped by rule, with lines and fixes, that finds the planted violations and does not flag the compliant constructs.
assertions: Flags the recursion in count_nodes (line 56) under rule 1.
Flags the goto in log_flush (lines 100 and 112) under rule 1.
Flags at least one of the loops with no static bound: the while loop at line 64 or the for loop at line 102, under rule 2.
Flags malloc in log_record (line 79) under rule 3, and the unchecked malloc result under rule 7.
Flags the ignored return values of fwrite (line 104) and fclose (line 106) under rule 7.
Flags the token-pasting macro DEFINE_COUNTER (line 15) and the variadic macro LOG (line 14) under rule 8.
Flags the unjustified #ifdef DEBUG_DUMP (line 107) under rule 8.
Flags the function pointer type log_cb or the indirect call on_record(r) (lines 25, 30, 87) under rule 9.
Flags the pointer-hiding typedef rec_ptr (line 24) under rule 9.
Flags the global g_tmp (line 31) under rule 6.
Does not report the (void)printf cast at line 110 or the c_assert macro's #e stringizing (lines 10-12) as violations.
Does not modify sensor_log.c.

evals.name: c-refactor-flood-fill
evals.prompt: evals/files/flood_fill.c is going into infusion pump firmware and our static analyzer rejects it because fill() is recursive. Refactor it so it complies with the JPL Power of Ten rules. Keep the flood_fill() signature and return values in flood_fill.h. Write the new flood_fill.c to the outputs directory.
evals.expected_output: A non-recursive flood fill that uses a fixed-capacity explicit stack in static or stack storage, with a bound derived from the grid size, the same results as the original, and checked parameters.
assertions: The refactored flood_fill.c contains no direct or indirect recursion.
The explicit work stack or queue has a compile-time capacity and is not heap-allocated; no malloc, VLA, or alloca.
The capacity is large enough for the worst case on a GRID_ROWS x GRID_COLS grid, or overflow returns a defined error and the reply states the limit.
Every loop has a provable bound.

For a full-grid fill, a single-cell region, a checkerboard, a start outside the grid, and new_color equal to the old color, the refactored function returns the same values and leaves the grid in the same state as the original.
The file compiles with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Wconversion with zero warnings.
The flood_fill signature in flood_fill.h is unchanged.

evals.name: cpp-write-command-dispatcher
evals.prompt: We're building the body control module for an automotive ECU in C++17 (gcc, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti, safety-critical, no heap after startup). Write command_dispatcher.hpp/.cpp: it receives CAN commands (uint8_t id, up to 8 data bytes, uint8_t dlc) and dispatches them to handlers for these ids: 0x10 set_headlights(level 0-3), 0x11 lock_doors(bool), 0x12 set_wiper(mode 0-4, speed 0-255), 0x13 request_status (fills a reply frame). Unknown ids and malformed payloads must be rejected with an error code. Include a test main.cpp.
evals.expected_output: A dispatcher with compile-time call targets (switch on id), no heap use, no exceptions, [[nodiscard]] status results, checked lengths and ranges, and a clean pedantic compile.
assertions: Dispatch uses a switch or direct calls; no std::function, function pointer, member function pointer, or virtual call through a base pointer selects the handler.
No new, delete, make_unique, make_shared, std::vector, std::string, std::map, or other allocating container in the dispatcher.
No throw, try, or catch.
Functions that return a status are marked [[nodiscard]] (on the function or on the status type), and every call site uses the result.
Each handler checks dlc and value ranges before using payload bytes, and rejects an unknown id with an error code.
Every loop has a compile-time bound.
No macro uses ## or __VA_ARGS__.
The files compile with g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Wconversion -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti with zero warnings, and the test program runs to completion.
The reply identifies which C++ guidance is an interpretation beyond the paper's C rules, or does not claim that the paper itself forbids C++-specific features.

evals.name: cpp-review-path-planner
evals.prompt: Review evals/files/path_planner.cpp from our rover mobility software against Holzmann's Power of Ten rules. I need a list of violations with line numbers and suggested fixes for the code review. Don't edit the file.
evals.expected_output: A review that maps the paper's rules to C++ features (exceptions, heap-allocating containers, virtual dispatch, std::function) and finds the planted violations without flagging compliant code.
assertions: Flags the recursion in depth() (line 87) under rule 1.
Flags the throw in step() (line 76) as non-local control flow under rule 1, or otherwise as a violation.
Flags the unbounded while loop in trace() (line 94), including the possible overrun of out, under rule 2.
Flags path_.push_back (line 78) as heap allocation after initialization under rule 3.
Flags std::make_unique (line 60) or the unique_ptr storage as heap allocation under rule 3.
Flags the ignored add_obstacle result (line 121) under rule 7.
Flags the token-pasting macro FIELD (line 11) under rule 8.
Flags virtual dispatch through Obstacle (lines 31, 69, or 106) and the std::function listener (lines 51, 81) as indirect calls under rule 9.
Does not report the static_assert at line 16 or the range-for over std::array at line 104 as violations.
Does not modify path_planner.cpp.

evals.name: cpp-refactor-tlv-parser
evals.prompt: evals/files/tlv_parser.hpp and tlv_parser.cpp parse nested TLV telemetry frames on our spacecraft's command and data handling board. It now has to meet the JPL Power of Ten rules and build with -fno-exceptions. Refactor it. You may change the API, but keep the parsing semantics (paths, values, and which frames are errors). Write the new tlv_parser.hpp and tlv_parser.cpp to the outputs directory, plus a test that shows old and new give the same results.
evals.expected_output: A parser without recursion, exceptions, or heap allocation: an explicit bounded nesting stack, fixed-capacity output with an error when full, status codes, and tests that compare against the original.
assertions: The new parser contains no recursion.
The new parser contains no throw, try, or catch, and compiles with -fno-exceptions.
The new parser does not use std::vector, std::string, new, or other heap allocation; output goes to fixed-capacity or caller-provided storage.
Nesting depth and output count have named compile-time limits, and exceeding them returns a distinct error status.
Every loop has a provable bound.
Functions that return a status are [[nodiscard]] or return a [[nodiscard]] type.

For valid frames (flat, nested, empty container, zero-length value) the new parser yields the same paths and values as the original, and for truncated headers and truncated values it reports an error where the original threw.
The new files compile with g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Wconversion -fno-exceptions with zero warnings.
